results.summary: One first-hand peak page for this south-side route says it is easiest in late spring (snow over the brush, snowmelt for water), an oven in mid-summer and possibly an ordeal for lack of water in late summer and fall, which backs the header's spring window; best_season and seasonal_guidance, which call August optimal, are rewritten to match.
results.evidence: Archived peak page, 'When to Climb': 'Davis might well be easiest in late Spring, when snow still suppresses some of the brush, and snowmelt provides water ... almost entirely south-facing; it would be an oven in mid-summer. In late Summer or Fall lack of water might make it an ordeal. We did it over the first weekend in January.'

ops.expect: Late July through mid-September gives the most reliable snow-free scrambling on the upper mountain and summit ridge; snow, moats, and cornices can linger into July on the shadier saddle and upper gullies. Some parties instead climb it in late May-June as a steep snow route while the approach brush is still snow-covered, and it has been climbed in winter during stable high-pressure windows by strong, experienced parties.
ops.value: Late spring is the easiest time: snow still covers much of the brush and snowmelt gives water on the way up. The route faces south almost the whole way, so mid-summer is very hot, and by late summer and fall the lack of water makes it an ordeal. It has also been climbed in winter during stable spells by strong, experienced parties.

expect.optimalWindow: Mid-July through September, once approach snow has melted out;

July.reason: Approach snow is often still lingering in shaded gullies and on the upper mountain early in the month; brushy lower approach can still be wet

August.reason: Most reliable window - approach typically fully melted out, driest rock, most stable access along the highway corridor

September.reason: Stable early in the month with continued dry rock; increasing chance of early-season snow and shortening daylight later in the month

value.optimalWindow: Late spring, while snow still covers the brush and snowmelt provides water

May.reason: Snow still suppresses the brush and snowmelt gives water on the south-facing slopes

July.reason: Mid-summer heat on an almost entirely south-facing route, with the brush fully exposed

August.reason: Hot and increasingly short of water on the way up

September.reason: Late-season lack of water can make the long climb an ordeal

results.evidence: Park route description: 'follows the Glacier Basin Trail (3.5 miles) to the Glacier Basin Campground ... at around 6,400 feet ... start up climber's right towards St. Elmo's Pass (7,500 feet)'; 'trailhead to Thumb Rock (approximately 8 miles and 6,500 feet of gain)'. No mileage to the pass itself.

results.summary: No source states a trailhead-to-summit time for Rock Mountain by Trail #1587; sources give only round-trip times (about 6.75-7.5 h), and the cleared 8.5 h was the car-to-car total.
results.evidence: Trail listings give the full out-and-back time; trip reports checked give no ascent time.

results.summary: The club route page gives 'Trailhead to Summit 5-6' hours, a range rather than a single figure; picking a number inside it would be computed, so summitTimeHrs stays null (the row's schedule already shows the summit at +5.5 h, inside that range).
results.evidence: Club route page for the Southwest Face: 'Times: 5-6 hr trailhead to summit'; trip profile 'Trailhead to Summit 5-6 | 3,400 ft; Summit to Trailhead 4-5'.

results.summary: No source states a one-way distance from the Stuart Lake trailhead to the col; sources give the trail to Colchuck Lake (4 mi) and then about an hour of cairned path above the dam, with no mileage.
results.evidence: Approach listing: 2,500 ft from the lake, about an hour from the dam to the col, no distance; trail pages give 4 mi to Colchuck Lake. The cleared 17.06 km was the round trip.

results.summary: The boulder's own listing states the approach from the North Fork Sauk trailhead is about 8 miles, so dist_km is filled with 8 mi converted to 12.87 km.
results.evidence: Boulder listing: 'Approach is from the standard North Fork of the Sauk river, same as that for Glacier Peak. It's about 8 miles.' The cleared 0.97 km was a boulder-session distance, not the approach.
